# Tempest Lords · Book II, pp. 398–411
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	398
P	They were, perhaps, the first of the <b>Makers</b> (page 264). They charted the seas and the stars. They leashed the elements to their will. They built mighty ships and flying castles, sailed forth from their island home and conquered. All who stood against them were reduced to ash and glass and slag.
P	The pride of the Tempest Lords was warranted, but their hubris led to their fall. They sought to tear their entire homeland free from the earth, to set it floating above the world they ruled.
P	They failed. Calamity followed.
P	The seas boiled and belched forth horrors.
P	Fire rained from the sky. Their island capital sank beneath the waves, and the spine of their empire was shattered. Civil war erupted. Colonies rebelled.
P	The Tempest Lords who survived were scattered to the winds. Some tried to restore the empire, but met violent ends at the hands of rivals or would-be subjects.
P	Soon, only a few Tempest Lords remained, enigmas even among other Makers.
P	One of these survivors, Stormcatcher, made her way to the <b>the Flats</b> (page 126), beyond even the most far-flung of the empire's old outposts. There, between four other nations of Makers, she built her tower. And when the horrors of the <b>Things</b> <b>Below</b> (page 412) were set loose upon the world, Stormcatcher's tower—what folks now call the <b>Ruined Tower</b> (page 332)—was the last of the Makers' enclaves to fall.
H2	Language and names
HR
P	Tempest Lord writing was ideogrammatic (characters represent ideas, not sounds), and they spoke a primordial language—all who heard it understood it as their native tongue. As such, the names of Tempest
P	Lords are rendered as descriptions, titles, or honorifics.
P	Example names: Brinedrinker, Eyes-Like-Lightning, Fardweller, Foehammer, Lightning-Is-Her-Spear, His-Smile-Isa-Harbor, Mind-Like-Fire, Moonspeaker, Oarbreaker, Rainchaser, Soother-Of-Waves, Sparkspitter, Squalltalker, Starfinder, Taller-Than-Masts, Voice-of-Thunder, Wavecutter, Waymaker, Windwalker
P	When other Makers spoke or wrote of them, they used their own tongue. Windwalker was called <i>Vetrodokha</i> by the <b>Green</b> <b>Lords</b> (page 210) and <i>Avaelkerzhaer</i> by the <b>Stone Lords</b> (page 382).

H3	Scars of unchecked power
P	For example:
B	A crater, lousy with fulgurites and shards of glass
B	A fractal, branching pattern etched in a bare expanse of stone
B	A rune-etched menhir or large hunk of <b>makerglass</b> (page 388), near which some fundamental law or force (time, gravity, space, light, etc.) is warped
B	A barren stretch of glass pebbles, strangely colored and always warm
B	The <b>vitrified</b> (page 408) remains of a Maker, a monster, a small army, etc. Crude glass shapes hinting at what they once were, flash-frozen in time Places scarred by such power might very well be <b>radioactive</b> (page 407), <b>haunted</b> <b>sites</b> (page 72), and/or corrupted by <b>the</b> <b>Things Below</b> (page 412).

H3	Fragments of a ship or sky-island
P	For example:
B	A ship's hull, mostly buried but somehow still intact
B	A torn sail of <b>aetherium</b> (page 404) mesh, strapped to a rusty metal cross
B	Strange objects, strewn about and long-buried: a crumpled brass cylinder, an etched metal disk, an oversized ship's wheel, a rudder, etc.
B	A rocky outcrop, the stone alien to the surrounding terrain, tilted at an odd angle
B	A cracked slab of granite, big as the granary and shot through with aetherium, floating a few feet above the ground and spinning listlessly
B	Slabs of worked stone: broken, buried, and scattered, like a child's toy dashed from impossible heights
H3	Enigmatic structures
P	For example:
B	Iron spires, like hollow rusted trees, placed in a line across the landscape
B	A black cube the size of a house; when lightning strikes, the earth lights up for miles with glowing lines that fade over the next few minutes
B	Stone plinths along a ridge line, some of them topped with 6-foot-tall sculptures, like tulips, spinning in the breeze
B	Copper cylinders, each maybe 8 feet tall and caked in verdigris; mostly buried in white and chalky soil
B	Megaliths, etched with ideographs that describe the motions of the stars
B	A bronze plaque upon a stone slab, the only notable feature for miles; untouched by lichen; deeply etched ideographs begin with the phrase, "This is not a place of honor"

H3	A ruin
P	Pick or roll for themes (page 399), structure, purpose, architectural elements, and condition. Place the ruin in an appropriate terrain (see page 126 for the <b>Flats</b> and page 350 for the <b>South</b> <b>Manmarch</b>, but Tempest Lords ranged far and wide). Populate it with <b>lingering signs</b> (page 400), <b>artifacts</b> (page 406) and/or <b>dangers</b> (page 407) of the Tempest Lords or the appropriate region.
P	1d12 structure
HR
P	1-2 Cluster of smaller buildings around some central feature
P	3 Single, larger building (block, dome, ziggurat, etc.)
P	4 Bunker/vault carved into the stone
P	5 Platform/amphitheater/terrace(s)
P	6 Tower/spire
P	7-9 Sky-island, crashed/grounded (and roll d6 again)
P	10-11 Sky-island, afloat but anchored/ fixed over a particular place (and roll d6 again)
P	12 Sky-island, free-floating across the landscape (and roll d6 again)
P	1d12 purpose
HR
P	1-2 Dwelling (home, barracks, dormitory, etc.)
P	3-4 Infrastructure (cistern, sewer, lighthouse, harbor, etc.)
P	5-6 Storage (vault, batteries, warehouse, library, museum, etc.)
P	7-8 Production (generator, workshop, shipworks, factory, farm, etc.)
P	9-10 Study/Experimentation (laboratory, observatory, orrery, etc.)
P	11-12 Enigma (magical device, artistic endeavor, etc.)
P	1d12 architectural elements
HR
P	1-2 Metal beams/cables/lattices/trusses
P	3-4 Open spaces: shafts, atriums, vaulted ceilings, overlooks, windows, skylights
P	5-6 Lines of power: <b>aetherium inlays</b> (page 341), runes, conduits, nodes, currents
P	7-8 Stylized mosaics/statuary: geometric patterns, fractals, celestial bodies, angelic beings, ships
P	9-10 Brass fixtures, pipes and pumps, water and steam, gears and flywheels
P	11-12 Verticality: standing stones, menhirs, obelisks, towers, spires, masts Most Maker-ruins are sized for giants—people two or even three times as tall as humans—but often with smaller-scale rooms, passages, and so forth for their servants.
P	1d12 condition
HR
P	1-4 Shattered and laid waste by time, disaster, or vandalism; mostly buried, overgrown, collapsed; its purpose unrecognizable
P	5-8 Crumbling, largely buried, overgrown, or hidden away
P	9-10 Buried, overgrown, or hidden, but mostly intact
P	11-12 Fully visible and strangely well-preserved For more examples, see the <b>Ruined Tower</b> (page 332).

H2	Aetherium
HR
P	An alloy of copper and lightning. Pure aetherium is light, soft, and ductile (similar to tin), but the Tempest Lords and <b>Forge</b> <b>Lords</b> (page 156) could further alloy it or manipulate it with magic to have a wide range of properties and uses.
P	Pick or roll for form and characteristic.
P	<b>1d12</b> form
HR
P	1-3 Raw material (ingot/spool of wire/ rod/plate/lamé/shard/etc.)
P	4-5 Enigmatic shape (torus/orb/tube/ hoop/runes/etc.), its purpose unclear
P	6-7 Mundane object (tool/vessel/ lantern/etc.), though perhaps not recognized as such
P	8-9 Art or decoration (jewel/statue/ inlay/torc/amulet/ring/etc.)
P	10 Clothing/armor (robe/tunic/apron/ cuirass/brigandine/etc.)
P	11 Weapon (spear/arrow/sword/maul/ shield/trident/wand/etc.)
P	12 Construction (archway/truss/beam/ door/plating/pipes/etc.), likely
P	<i>immobile</i>
P	Consider rolling 1d6 to inform size/scale.
P	1d12 characteristic
HR
P	1 Breathtakingly beautiful
P	2 Hard and strong as bronze
P	3 Absorbs/stores/discharges/ transforms an elemental force
P	4 Suppresses/repels/directs/impedes a particular element/force
P	5 Vibrates in ways that interact with spirits/magic
P	6 Extremely light/levitates/defies or reverses gravity
P	7 Attunes to another item/locale, for communication/detection
P	8 Roll 1d8 twice
P	9 Unstable, prone to discharge/failure (<i>dangerous</i>) and roll d8 again
P	10 Relatively soft/ductile/malleable
P	(<i>crude</i>)
P	11-12 Roll again with 1d8, but it becomes unstable and/or soft (as above) after any serious use

H3	Making aetherium
P	A clever arcanist might rediscover the process of making aetherium. To do so, you must…
C	Study a largely-intact aetherium crucible for a few weeks
C	Study both active and depleted aetherium for a few weeks
C	Consult a knowledgeable metalsmith (or be one yourself)
C	Acquire the appropriate chemics (Value 0) and a sizeable mass of copper (Value 1, <i>immobile</i>)
C	Devise some way to introduce lightning to molten copper
C	Risk injury, fire, destruction, and failure
P	When you <b><i>meet all the requirements</i></b>, you can transform a purse of coppers (Value ◇
P	0) and the appropriate chemics (Value 0) into an ingot or casting of pure aethe-◇ rium (<i>magical</i>, <i>crude</i>, possibly dangerous,
P	Value 1 to those-who-know). The process is risky; you are Defying Danger each time you undertake it.
P	To imbue aetherium with one of the characteristics above, you'll need access to a trove of Tempest Lord or Forge Lord lore, at least. Beyond that, <b>Make a Plan</b> with the GM.
TH	steading improvement
C	<b>AETHERIUM CRUCIBLE</b>
P	Requires all of the following:
C	Learning the process of <b>making</b> <b>aetherium</b> (at left)
C	Learning to imbue aetherium with at least one special characteristic
C	A reliable means of capturing, storing, and directing lightning that strikes the Stone
C	Securing a steady supply of the chemics needed to make aetherium
C	Securing a steady supply of copper
C	An exceptional smith who knows the secrets of aetherium
P	When you <b><i>mark all the requirements</i></b>, add "Aetherium Crucible" to the Resources list and the map. As long as you trade aetherium to the outside world, increase Prosperity by 1.
P	Henceforth, small amounts of raw aetherium (<i>magical</i>, Value 1) are commonly available in Stonetop, and you have advantage to <b>Trade &</b>
P	<b>Barter</b> for the aetherium items with special characteristics (+2 Value).

H3	Aetherium urn
P	◇, <i>magical</i>, <i>dangerous</i>
P	The lid is held fast by no apparent means.
P	It takes some effort to pry open and eagerly snaps back into place.
P	When <b><i>the urn is open and empty</i></b>, it draws raw elemental force into it like a lodestone draws iron. With the lid in place, the force is safely stored. If the urn is damaged or dented (not hard), any stored force escapes, violently.
HR
ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	Bronze ring
P	◇, <i>magical</i>, <i>fireproof</i>, hours About 8 inches in diameter, an inch thick throughout, scorched and smeared with ash. A button protrudes, with a Tempest Lord glyph that might mean "stubborn."
P	When you <b><i>find the ring</i></b>, it has enough power to run for 1d4-1 hours.
P	When you <b><i>press the button</i></b>, the ring fixes in place, defying gravity. It simply will not budge. The effect ends if the ring is bent or broken, or when it runs out of power.
P	There's no obvious way to end the effect early. When <b><i>the ring runs out of power</i></b>, the button pops out and the effect ends.
P	When <b><i>you heat the ring in a forge or kiln</i></b> for about eight hours, it gains an hour of use (up to 3 hours).

H2	Dangers
HR
H3	Monsters and entities
B	A <b>thunder drake</b> (page 135) or <b>luglfsk</b> (page 92), drawn to aetherium
B	<b>Ghosts</b> (page 76) or <b>revenants</b> (page 80), victims of the Tempest Lord's experiments, callousness, or wrath

HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Radiation
P	Sometimes, the Tempest Lords unleashed such terrible power that it poisoned all it touched: soil, bone, stone, metal. Poisoned them all so deeply that now, still, centuries and centuries later, those things poison all that draws near.
P	Such poisonous places are often corrupted by the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412). But even when they are not, they are dangerous.
P	• Point out flora or fauna, stunted and strange
P	• Make their skin itch, make them feel unwell
P	• Inflict a debility that refuses to go away
P	• Have symptoms appear (or return) hours or days after exposure
P	• Have symptoms linger or worsen, perhaps for months
P	PCs or NPCs exposed to such radiation are prone to developing terrible, wasting illness, months or years later. Write this up as a threat (an <i>affliction</i>).
PAGE	408
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Vitrification
P	A few Tempest Lords could call up a bolt of power so raw and potent that it would turn whatever it touched into glass.
P	It was dangerous for even them to use, but no foe could stand against it.
P	It's possible that some device still exists that can unleash this sort of power. If so, treat it as a threat (a <i>MacGuffin</i>; <b>Instinct</b> to tempt people into using it). It would
P	require vast amounts of energy and involve extraordinary risks.
P	When you <b><i>are struck by a vitrifying bolt</i></b>, reduce your HP to 0 and roll +CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, you merely suffer terrible burns and will soon be at Death's Door; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you and your possessions are turned to jagged glass, but you might be restored; <b>on a 6-</b>, you die but your corpse, your soul, and your possessions are also turned into jagged glass—should the vitrification be reversed, it's as though you rolled a 6- on Death's Door.
P	Vitrification can be reversed, but you must decide how it's done. Perhaps it involves:
E	vast amounts of power and great risk;
E	a sympathetic link to the victim, or whatever vitrified them in the first place;
E	the intervention of a powerful <b>god</b> (page 178) or <b>primordial entity</b> (page 298);
E	spilling the life-blood of your kin upon the jagged glass;
E	a spell of transference, where someone else becomes vitrified instead;
E	a spiritwalker releasing the vitrified soul, and guiding it to a suitable vessel;
E	something different for each victim, or for each source of vitrification;
E	some combination of the above; or
E	something else entirely.
ICON	icons/spirit.svg
H3	Elemental vortex
P	Picture a filigree sphere of aetherium, maybe 6 inches across, a glowing mote swirling at its center. This device—called a matrix—binds an <b>elemental spirit</b> (page 360) and absorbs a particular force, with which the spirit is able to manifest a swirling vortex.
P	A spirit bound to a matrix must follow any orders given in the Tempest Lord's primordial language. As few alive can give them such orders, any matrices encountered will likely be acting on orders from centuries ago.
P	<b>Power and size:</b> Each matrix absorbs a particular type of power, and current HP of its vortex reflects its current power.
P	As a vortex gains or loses HP, its size, armor, and damage change as well. At 0 HP, it dissipates and its matrix falls to the ground, inert until it absorbs more HP.
P	Pick or roll to determine a vortex's starting size, HP, Armor, and Damage.
P	1d12 hp stats
HR
P	1-4 1 to 5 <i>tiny</i>; Armor 1;
P	Damage d8-2 (<i>hand</i>)
P	5-7 6 to 11 <i>small</i>; Armor 2;
P	Damage d8 (<i>hand</i>)
P	8-9 12 to 18 Armor 2;
P	Damage d10 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>)
P	10-11 19 to 23 <i>large</i>; Armor 3;
P	Damage d10+3 (<i>hand</i>,
P	<i>close</i>, <i>reach</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	12 24 to 28 <i>huge</i>; Armor 3;
P	Damage d10+5 (<i>hand</i>,
P	<i>close</i>, <i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
PAGE	409
P	<b>Attacking the matrix:</b> A matrix itself has only 3 HP. If reduced to 0 HP, the spirit within escapes, dealing the vortex's current damage (+<i>area</i>, one range tag greater than normal).
P	When <b><i>a PC tries to strike the matrix inside</i></b> <b><i>an active vortex</i></b>, the vortex's Armor applies. Also, tell them the requirements and/ or consequences. such as:
B	You'll have disadvantage to Clash/ Let Fly/deal damage
B	You'll need to create or wait for an opening, where the matrix is exposed
B	You'll need to get in close/let it engulf you
B	You'll need a longer/heavier/<i>magical</i> weapon
B	You'll risk losing/ruining your weapon
B	You'll suffer its attack, no matter what
P	Pick options based on the nature of the vortex, the PC's weapon, and the rest of their fictional positioning. The larger the vortex, the harder it is to strike the matrix.

H3	Earth vortex
P	<i>Solitary</i>, size by HP, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>,
P	<i>amorphous</i>, <i>grumpy</i>, <i>clumsy</i>
P	<b>HP</b> varies; <b>Armor</b> by HP, +1 (made of rock)
P	<b>Damage</b> smash (damage and tags by HP)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> half damage from stabbing or slashing weapons (unless <i>magical</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to topple and undermine
P	• Manifest a churning mass out of nearby earth, sand, and rocks
P	• Pin a smaller foe (+<i>grabby</i>)
P	• Grind a pinned foe, dealing damage w/advantage (+<i>messy</i>)
P	• Ruin a sturdy object or structure (costs 1d4 HP)
P	• Shake the earth (+<i>area</i>, +<i>forceful</i>, one range greater than normal; costs 1d4 HP)
P	An earth matrix absorbs power from pressure, blunt force, and seismic activity.
P	It gains 1d4 HP from a week buried under earth or stone, from being at the bottom of a rockslide or cave-in, or from touching the ground during a major earthquake (not one it created).
P	When you <b><i>strike an earth matrix with a</i></b> <b><i>bludgeoning attack</i></b>, it takes no damage. If the blow was forceful and its vortex has 10 HP or less, it gains 1 HP. (The vortex itself has no such immunities, smash away!)

P	• Set nearby combustibles alight
P	• Manifest a vortex out of nearby fire, cinder, smoke, and ash
P	• Extinguish fires, absorbing their power (<i>near</i>, <i>area</i>)
P	• Engulf a smaller foe (+<i>messy</i>, +ignores armor)
P	• Fling flames (+<i>near</i>; costs 1d4 HP)
P	• Leap across a barrier (but lose 1d4 HP)
P	A fire vortex absorbs power from heat and flames. It gains 1d4 HP by spending a day in an oven or an hour in a forge or kiln, or by absorbing a raging fire.
P	When you <b><i>target a fire vortex or its matrix</i></b> <b><i>with</i></b> <b>magical</b> <b><i>fire or heat</i></b>, it takes no damage. If the vortex has 18 HP or less, it gains 1d4 HP instead.

P	• Tear the lightning from unattended aetherium, gaining 1d4 HP
P	A lightning vortex absorbs power from, well, lightning. When it is struck by lightning (mundane or <i>magical</i>), it gains HP instead of taking damage.

H3	Water vortex
P	<i>Solitary</i>, size by HP, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>,
P	<i>amorphous</i>, <i>relentless</i>, <i>callous</i>
P	<b>HP</b> varies; <b>Armor</b> by HP
P	<b>Damage</b> pummel (damage and tags by HP)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> harmed only by <i>magical</i> weapons, cold, or <i>forceful</i> blunt attacks <b>Instinct</b> to adjust, flow, and adapt
P	• Manifest a churning wave out of water it touches
P	• Vanish into/burst out of a body of water
P	• Engulf a smaller foe (+<i>grabby</i>, see below)
P	• Surge past foes, dragging them off their feet (+<i>area</i>, +<i>forceful</i>, costs 1d4 HP)
P	• Move across a porous surface (costs 1d4 HP)
P	A water matrix absorbs power from currents, tides, waves, and falling water. It gains 1d4 HP from a few days in a flowing stream, a few hours in a rushing river, or a few minutes in rapids or a major waterfall.
P	When you <b><i>are engulfed by a water vortex</i></b>, hold 1d4 Breath. When you <b><i>make a move</i></b> <b><i>while engulfed</i></b>, and that move involves a roll, spend 1 Breath or mark a debility after rolling. If you can't do either, you drown and are at Death's Door.

H3	Wind vortex
P	<i>Solitary</i>, size by HP, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>,
P	<i>amorphous</i>, <i>restless</i>, <i>fickle</i>
P	<b>HP</b> varies; <b>Armor</b> by HP
P	<b>Damage</b> lashing grit/debris (damage and tags by HP, but w/disadvantage)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> flies, harmed only by <i>magical</i> weapons, salt, or lead
P	<b>Instinct</b> to play
P	• Manifest a vortex of churning wind, grit, and debris
P	• Engulf a smaller foe (+<i>grabby</i>)
P	• Carry an engulfed foe aloft (costs 1d4 HP)
P	• Fling objects (+near; costs 1d4 HP)
P	• Flee when hurt, frightened, or bored
P	A wind matrix absorbs power from moving air. It gains 1d4 HP from weeks exposed to normal weather, an hour in high winds, or a minute or so in a tornado.
P	When you <b><i>strike a wind vortex with a salt</i></b> <b><i>or lead</i></b>, it takes 1d4 damage from a handful, 2d4 damage from a item, and 3d4 ◇ damage from a ◇◇ item or amount.
